intro: Retrieved passages compete for a limited context window. A long high-scoring passage can leave room for only a few others.
task: Select candidate indices greedily by descending relevance score, accepting each only if its token cost fits the remaining budget.
requirements: costs is a nonempty vector of positive integer values. scores is a same-length finite nonnegative vector. budget is a nonnegative integer excluding booleans.
Rank by descending score, breaking ties by original index. Skip a candidate that does not fit and continue scanning later candidates.
Return selected indices as a Python list in selection order. This is a relevance-first greedy policy, not an optimal knapsack solver or score-per-token ranking.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Sort indices by (-score, original index), then maintain a remaining budget.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: An oversized candidate means continue, not break; a later smaller one may fit.

explanation: A context budget turns retrieval ranking into a selection problem. Relevance order alone is insufficient because every selected passage consumes capacity.
This simple policy preserves relevance priority and skips oversized candidates. It is deterministic and easy to inspect, but can miss combinations with higher total relevance.

Construct two medium passages whose combined score exceeds one large passage. Explain when you might prefer a different selection policy, and where you would reserve tokens for the prompt and generated answer.
